comparison: Both evaluate the foundational scRNA-seq data quality and cell counting methodology (C6, C35-C37). OpenEval focuses on technical metrics and manual segmentation, while peer reviewers emphasize the overall value of the transcriptomic resource and validation approach. Both find the data well-supported.

Both address the primary clustering results (C7, C38-C44). OpenEval provides detailed assessment of the 19 clusters with UMAP and marker validation, while peer reviewers praise the overall quality and in situ validation approach. Both find the clustering well-supported.

Both evaluate cellular composition claims (C8-C14). OpenEval assesses the quantification methodology and ISH validation in detail, while peer reviewers emphasize the value of spatial information and absolute cell numbers. Both find the composition data well-supported.

Both address muscle cell characterization (C45-C57, C150). OpenEval provides detailed assessment of marker validation and spatial organization, while peer reviewers praise the in situ validation and marker counting approach. Both find the muscle characterization well-supported.

Both evaluate neural cell populations (C58-C80, C158). OpenEval provides comprehensive assessment of five neural clusters with subclustering and marker validation, while peer reviewers affirm the quality of cell type characterization and validation. Both find the neural diversity well-supported.

Both address penetration gland cell characterization using plate-based scRNA-seq (C81-C83, C148-C149). OpenEval assesses the alternative methodology and findings, while peer reviewers explicitly praise the recognition of methodological bias and application of a second method. Both find this approach well-supported.

Both evaluate ciliary plate and submuscular cell findings (C84-C86, C146-C147). OpenEval assesses the novel submuscular cell discovery and methodological insights about unsorted samples, while peer reviewers praise the recognition of isolation bias and methodological adaptation. Both find these discoveries well-supported.

Both address tegumental cell characterization (C87-C90, C170-C172). OpenEval assesses marker validation and spatial distribution, while peer reviewers affirm the quality of cell type characterization and validation work. Both find the tegument identification well-supported.

Both evaluate protonephridial system characterization (C91-C95). OpenEval assesses marker conservation and spatial organization, while peer reviewers affirm the validation approach and spatial information. Both find the excretory system characterization well-supported.

Both address parenchymal cell populations (C96-C100). OpenEval notes the marker validation and spatial distribution, while peer reviewers affirm the validation work and cell type characterization. Both find the parenchyma identification well-supported.

Both evaluate stem cell populations and sex-based clustering (C101-C115). OpenEval provides detailed assessment of marker validation and sex-biased expression, while peer reviewers explicitly highlight this as an unexpected and interesting finding. Both find the stem cell characterization well-supported.

Both address sex-biased gene expression and dosage compensation (C19-C20, C108, C181-C183). OpenEval assesses the clustering evidence and dosage compensation inference, while peer reviewers call this particularly unexpected and interesting. Both find the sex-biased findings well-supported.

Both evaluate the absence of cell division in miracidia (C116-C118). OpenEval assesses the EdU incorporation data and inference about proliferation pause, while peer reviewers accept this finding within their overall positive assessment. Both find this observation well-supported.

Both address molecular characterization of stem cell states (C119-C125, C175). OpenEval assesses the STRING analysis, differential expression, and GO analysis supporting activation state differences, while peer reviewers accept these interpretations without challenge. Both find the molecular characterization well-supported.

Both evaluate tegument lineage trajectory (C17, C126-C132, C173-C174). OpenEval assesses the RNA velocity analysis and marker dynamics, while peer reviewers accept the trajectory analysis and lineage conclusions without concerns. Both find the tegument trajectory well-supported.

Both address Kappa population and germline fate (C18, C133-C138, C178-C179). OpenEval assesses germline marker expression and trajectory predictions, while peer reviewers accept the germline interpretations without challenge. Both find the germline identity claims well-supported, though OpenEval notes they remain predictions.

Both evaluate methodological insights about cell isolation bias (C144-C147). OpenEval assesses the observation of stem cell overrepresentation and benefits of unsorted samples, while peer reviewers explicitly praise the recognition of isolation bias and methodological adaptation. Both find these insights well-supported.

Both address muscle populations and axial patterning roles (C150-C157). OpenEval assesses the correspondence to muscle types and inferences about patterning, while peer reviewers accept these interpretations without concerns. Both find the patterning hypotheses well-supported.

Both evaluate the utility of miracidium as a model system and conserved developmental programs (C139-C140, C188-C191). OpenEval assesses the simplicity argument and cell count comparisons, while peer reviewers emphasize the value as a transcriptomic resource for the field. Both find these conclusions well-supported.

Both address conserved transcriptional programs and somatic cell fate (C188-C191). OpenEval assesses the inference about stage-specific somatic cells and conserved programs, while peer reviewers affirm the value of the resource and accept these conclusions. Both find the interpretations well-supported.

Both address the methodological approach for gland cells (C148-C149). OpenEval explains the absence from 10X data and use of plate-based scRNA-seq, while peer reviewers praise the recognition of methodological bias. Both find this approach well-supported.

Both discuss tegument cell biology and developmental program (C170-C174). OpenEval assesses STRING analysis and consistency with ultrastructure, while peer reviewers affirm the validation work. Both find the tegument biology claims well-supported.

OpenEval evaluates background claims about S. mansoni biology and schistosomiasis epidemiology (C1-C5, C21-C27) as well-established facts. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focused on novel findings rather than contextual background.

OpenEval evaluates summary claims about neuronal diversity and trajectory analysis (C15-C18). While peer reviewers address related trajectory findings in R13 and R14, they do not specifically evaluate these summary claims as a distinct group.

OpenEval evaluates literature context claims (C28-C32) as accurate summaries of prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focused on the study's novel contributions rather than literature review.

OpenEval evaluates background on miracidium biology from ultrastructural studies (C33-C34). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focused on molecular characterization rather than historical context.

OpenEval evaluates neural system discussion claims (C158-C162) about abundance, heterogeneity, and functional predictions. While peer reviewers affirm neural characterization in R3, they do not specifically evaluate these interpretive discussion points.

OpenEval rates claims about submuscular cell function (C163-C165) as UNCERTAIN due to lack of functional validation, noting these are reasonable hypotheses. Peer reviewers do not specifically evaluate these functional speculation claims.

OpenEval evaluates ciliary plate biology discussion (C166-C169) as well-supported by citations and expression data. Peer reviewers do not specifically evaluate these discussion points about ciliary plate biology.

OpenEval evaluates interpretation of stem cell activation states (C175-C177), finding the different activation states well-supported but proliferation order speculative. Peer reviewers do not specifically evaluate these interpretive claims separately.

OpenEval rates early germline segregation claims (C178-C180) as UNCERTAIN, noting the interpretation of spliced-only transcripts is speculative with alternative explanations. Peer reviewers do not specifically evaluate these speculative mechanistic claims.

OpenEval evaluates discussion of sex-biased findings novelty and context (C183-C187) as well-supported. While peer reviewers affirm the sex-biased findings in R10, they do not specifically evaluate these contextual discussion points.
